# Idle and stale resource reports in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers read-only administrator reports in the RHOAI web console
that surface idle and stale resources per project, so administrators can see
where capacity is being held unused and reclaim it with confidence. Two
reports are built on one console reporting surface: an idle-workbench report
sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking, and a stale
pipeline-run report sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. Either
report can be exported as CSV.

## Scope

- Per-project idle-workbench report in the console listing, for each
  workbench: last activity (sourced from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking), owner, and reserved resources.
- Per-project stale pipeline-run report in the console listing completed
  pipeline runs older than a configurable age threshold, together with their
  retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Administrator-configurable stale-run age threshold for the pipeline-run
  report.
- CSV export of either report, matching the on-screen data.
- Console presentation is project-scoped (reports are viewed per data science
  project).
- Reporting is strictly read-only: no automated reclamation or deletion of
  resources, and no cost/chargeback calculations (both out of scope for the
  strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing activity, when an
  administrator opens the idle-workbench report, then the report lists each
  workbench with its last activity timestamp, its owner, and its reserved
  resources, and the last-activity values match the notebook controller's
  activity tracking.
- Given a project with completed pipeline runs, when an administrator opens
  the stale pipeline-run report, then the report lists completed runs older
  than the configured age threshold together with their retained artifacts,
  and the entries match Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Given the stale-run age threshold is configurable, when an administrator
  changes the threshold, then the stale pipeline-run report reflects the new
  threshold without requiring code changes.
- Given either report is displayed, when an administrator exports it, then a
  CSV file is produced whose rows match the on-screen report contents.
- Given the reports are used, when an administrator reviews cluster state,
  then no resources have been modified or deleted by the reporting feature
  (read-only reporting).
- Given a project with no idle workbenches or stale runs, when the reports
  are opened, then they render empty states without errors.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner,
  reserved resources) sourced from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking — covered by this epic.
- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
  configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines
  run metadata — covered by this epic.
- HLR-3 (P2): CSV export of either report — covered by this epic; bundled
  because it is a thin increment on the same report surface the P1 work
  builds, not an independently deferrable feature.

# Document the idle and stale resource reports and safe reclamation

## Description

This epic delivers product documentation for the console's idle and stale
resource reporting capability: what each report shows, where the data comes
from, how to configure the stale-run age threshold, how to export reports as
CSV, and how administrators can safely reclaim capacity based on the reports.
It is authored after the console reporting implementation is complete, so the
documentation describes the feature as actually built.

## Scope

- New documentation topics explaining the per-project idle-workbench report
  (last activity, owner, reserved resources) and the stale pipeline-run report
  (configurable age threshold, retained artifacts).
- Guidance on configuring the stale-run age threshold.
- Guidance on exporting either report as CSV.
- Safe manual reclamation steps for idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs
  — guidance for administrators acting on the reports; documentation must not
  imply automated reclamation (out of scope for this strategy).
- Screenshots and captions reflecting the reports as built.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the reporting capability is implemented, when the documentation is
  published, then topics exist that explain both reports, their per-project
  presentation, the configurable stale-run age threshold, and CSV export.
- Given an administrator wants to reclaim capacity, when they follow the
  documentation, then safe manual reclamation steps for idle workbenches and
  stale pipeline runs are described accurately.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented console
  reports, and any discrepancies found in review are corrected before
  publication.
- The documentation does not describe automated reclamation/deletion or
  cost/chargeback functionality (both out of scope).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps —
  covered by this epic.

# Decomposition: RHAISTRAT-9016 — Idle resource reporting in the web console

The strategy asks for two read-only administrator reports in the RHOAI web
console — idle workbenches per project and stale pipeline runs — plus CSV
export and documentation. The strategy explicitly states the underlying data
already exists (notebook controller activity tracking, Kubeflow Pipelines run
metadata) and lists no open questions, so the only active component is the web
console; the two data-source components are passive.

**Triage outcome:** not below-threshold. Although the code work is a single
component and team, the scope spans two architecturally distinct work streams
— console code implementation (HLR-1/2/3) and substantive documentation
authoring with new doc topics (HLR-4, including safe-reclamation guidance) —
which warrant separate PR review cycles. Full decomposition follows.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Idle and stale resource reports in the RHOAI web console | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 | Document the idle and stale resource reports and safe reclamation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Docs | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 — Idle and stale resource reports (Implementation, P1)"] --> E002["E002 — Documentation (docs-authoring, P2)"]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementation epics) | The documentation describes the reports as built (columns, thresholds, export behavior, reclamation steps); it cannot be authored or technically reviewed accurately before the console reporting implementation is complete. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Notes |
|-----|----------|------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Per-project idle-workbench report sourced from notebook controller activity tracking |
| HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Stale pipeline-run report sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata |
| HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | CSV export bundled with the reports: it is a thin increment on the same report UI surface and shares the reports' data, so it is not independently deferrable (Step 4 priority-split rule does not apply) |
| HLR-4 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 | Substantive new doc topics — separate work-product stream (docs-authoring) |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Boundary Decisions

- **HLR-1 + HLR-2 in one epic:** both reports are the same logical change —
  per-project idle/stale resource reporting — on the same component (web
  console), same team (RHOAI Dashboard), same work-product type (code), and
  the same console reporting surface. HLR-3 applies to "either report",
  further coupling the surface. Splitting would make two epics build the same
  reporting surface with an artificial serialization edge.
- **No Investigation epics:** the strategy lists "Open Questions: None", has
  no risks/assumptions tables, no pending reviews, no conditional ADRs. How
  the console reads last-activity timestamps and run metadata (exact API/CR
  surface) is an implementation detail the Dashboard team resolves when
  starting work — captured as acceptance criteria on E001, not a genuine
  unknown.
- **Passive components:** Notebook controller (canonical component
  `Notebooks`, owning team Workbenches) and Kubeflow Pipelines (canonical
  component `Data Science Pipelines`, owning team RHOAI Pipelines) need no
  code changes — the strategy states the data exists. Validation that the
  reports match those data sources is an acceptance criterion on E001; no
  separate validation epics since the consuming (Dashboard) team performs the
  validation.

## Component Mapping

| Strategy term | Canonical component | Status |
|---------------|---------------------|--------|
| RHOAI web console | Dashboard | Active — all code changes |
| Notebook controller | Notebooks | Passive — data source, no code changes |
| Kubeflow Pipelines | Data Science Pipelines | Passive — data source, no code changes |

All components exist in `.context/architecture-context/` (dashboard.md,
notebooks.md, data-science-pipelines.md); no new-component onboarding chain
is needed, and the Dashboard repo is already Konflux-onboarded.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections:** the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then Acceptance Criteria, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements. Epic acceptance criteria were derived from the
  HLRs; team assignments were taken from architecture context owning-team

- **Affected Components is a bare list** without owner/change columns; the
  active/passive classification above is inferred from the problem statement
  ("the data exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere").
- **Docs team assumption:** the strategy names no documentation owner; the
  `RHOAI Docs` team for the `Documentation` component is inferred from
  platform naming conventions.
- No priority inversions detected; no scope traps (out-of-scope items —
  automated reclamation and cost/chargeback — are respected in epic scope and
  docs acceptance criteria).
